# The four shaders that hung the GC7000 when our compiler built them

**Status (2026-10-11): closed.** These cases no longer hang. The i.MX8MP's
whole dEQP-GLES2 tree on main `32778b57` runs `shaders.algorithm.*` with our
compiler and has 0 failures (`tools/cts/STATUS.md`). The investigation is in
`driver/src/vivante/NOTES.md` and `tools/cts/RESULTS.md`. What follows is
the record as it was written while the hang was open.

`dEQP-GLES2.functional.shaders.algorithm.{hsl_to_rgb,rgb_to_hsl}_{vertex,fragment}`,
as dEQP actually sends them. They are here so the defect can be worked on
without a board: the GPU hang is reproducible from these four texts alone.

## What they are for

On the i.MX8MP, same driver and same GPU, the two `*_vertex` cases hang the
GC7000 when the shaders come from our in-process compiler, and all four pass
when they come from the reference compiler. The GLSL contains **no loop** --
`hsl_to_rgb` is a six-arm `if / else if` chain over `sextant`, `rgb_to_hsl` a
three-arm one -- so a program that never terminates is one we emitted.

Note which shader carries the work, because it is the whole point:

| case | vertex shader | fragment shader | hangs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hsl_to_rgb_vertex` | **the chain** | `gl_FragColor = vec4(v_color, 1.0);` | **yes** |
| `hsl_to_rgb_fragment` | passes `a_unitCoords` through | **the chain** | no |
| `rgb_to_hsl_vertex` | **the chain** | trivial | **yes** |
| `rgb_to_hsl_fragment` | trivial | **the chain** | no |

The same chain hangs in the vertex stage and not in the fragment stage.

## Provenance, and why these are byte-exact

They are not hand-copied. `es2fShaderAlgorithmTests.cpp` builds each case from
a fixed template in `createExpressionCase()` (`${PRECISION}` -> `mediump`), and
the body goes through `LineStream(1)`, which prefixes **one tab** to every line
-- so the body is tab-indented inside a space-indented `main()`. These files
were generated by applying that template rather than by retyping it.

The check that they are right is not that they compile. Every one of the four
came back from the shader server as `{"cached": true, "ok": true}`: the cache
key is a hash of the source text, and the only thing that had put these texts
in that cache was the board run of these same four cases. A cache hit is
byte-equality with what dEQP sent.

Regenerate with the snippet in `tools/cts/RESULTS.md` if the CTS version moves;
do not edit these by hand, and re-check the cache-hit property afterwards.
